flashcard_questions.q: What type of quantity is distance, which has size but no direction?
What type of quantity is displacement?
flashcard_questions.a: A vector — the straight-line distance from start to finish in a given direction.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation for uniform acceleration is used when the time is not known?
Which equation links speed, distance and time?
flashcard_questions.a: speed = distance ÷ time, or v = s ÷ t

flashcard_questions.q: How does velocity differ from speed?
flashcard_questions.a: Velocity is speed in a stated direction, which makes it a vector.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the approximate speed of a person walking?
What is the approximate speed of sound in air?
What does the gradient of a distance–time graph represent?
What motion does a horizontal line on a distance–time graph show?
How do you find the speed at one point on a curved distance–time graph?
flashcard_questions.a: Draw a tangent to the curve at that point and find its gradient.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the gradient of a velocity–time graph represent?
What does the area under a velocity–time graph represent?
Which equation links acceleration, change in velocity and time?
flashcard_questions.a: acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time taken, or a = (v − u) ÷ t

flashcard_questions.q: What is the unit of acceleration?
At what rate does an object in free fall accelerate near Earth's surface?
flashcard_questions.a: Approximately 9.8 m/s², often rounded to 10 m/s² in calculations.

notes: 15 cards: 2 term→definition (scalar, vector/displacement), 3 equation cards quoted verbatim (v = s ÷ t, a = (v − u) ÷ t, v² = u² + 2as), 4 value-and-unit cards (1.5 m/s walking, 330 m/s sound, 9.8 m/s² free fall, m/s² unit), 5 graph-interpretation cards across both graph types, 1 speed-versus-velocity distinction. Dropped the two worked-example answers and the remaining typical speeds (cycling, car, train, aeroplane) to stay inside 15 and avoid a run of near-identical value cards.
